thread.title: Lumentum: A Diversified Growth Opportunity - Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE)

author: Business Quant
title: Lumentum: A Diversified Growth Opportunity - Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE)
text:
It's no secret that the entire optical hardware and systems sector is going through a phase of transitory slowdown. Shares of prominent industry incumbents are substantially down compared to last year's levels as their data center and telecommunications clients abruptly slowed down their capital spending. But that doesn't leave investors with no options within the sector. Investors looking to enter the space can consider buying into Lumentum ( LITE ). Its shares haven't suffered major declines on a year-on-year basis (unlike some of its pure-play peers) and the company has diversified exposure to multiple segments that can potentially result in balanced growth over the years to come.
(Source: Bigstockphoto, Image license purchased by author)
Diversified Clientele Most companies operating within the networking hardware manufacturing segment tend to be specialized and cater to specific niches within their operating segments. This is evident by the fact that they rely on a handful of companies for most of their sales. For instance, Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ: AAOI ) and Neophotonics (NYSE: NPTN ) generate about 76% and 64% of their revenues from their top three customers alone, respectively.
Granted that having a huge exposure to a few customers can catapult the company's growth if its customers are ramping purchases aggressively. However, this strategy of over reliance can also backfire if the company's key customers abruptly slow down its rate of purchases. Apparently, this is what hurt Applied Optoelectronics and its shareholders over the past year. But Lumentum is different in this regard.
Lumentum has a relatively lower customer concentration risk compared to most of its industry peers. The chart attached below illustrates that the company generated about 49% of its revenues from its top three customers. Granted that this is still a high figure and Lumentum needs to further diversify its customer base, but the concentration risk is at least lower than what the industry is used to seeing, and definitely lower than its mentioned peers.
(Source: BusinessQuant.com)
This kind of customer diversity basically ensures that Lumentum's revenues are relatively stable and aren't as volatile. If there's any customer that's abruptly slowing down its rate of purchases, then evolving market dynamics may encourage other customers to hike their rate of purchases. Obviously, this is a statistics-based statement and doesn't have any predictive element attached to it.
That's also part of the reason why Lumentum's revenues haven't plunged by as much as some of the other names in the communications systems and hardware sector.
LITE Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts
Diversified Geographical Sales But that's not all. There's another factor working in Lumentum's favor that tends to stabilize its overall sales compared to some of its volatile peers - geographical diversification.
When companies have few customers accounting for the bulk of their revenues, then they also tend to have geographically concentrated sales. After all, their few customers would tend to have only a few shipping destinations. For instance, Neophotonics generates about 57% of its revenue from Chinese shipments alone.
This kind of a saturated geographical distribution of revenues can be a massive headwind for companies if there's any disruption in political ties with that particular country. For instance, if China were to hike or impose new tariffs on American-made components, then Neophotonics would be amongst the worst hit names.
This is where Lumentum differentiates itself once again. First of all, sales to Chinese shipping destinations accounted for only about 15% of its overall sales in the last quarter. So, the company is moderately exposed on a standalone basis, and not extremely, if political ties between China and the U.S deteriorated.
But besides China, Lumentum seems to have a myriad of shipping destinations that tend to diversify and mitigate the political and foreign exchange risk. I've attached a chart below for your reference. Note that China wasn't even a 10%-plus customer for the company in the prior quarter.
This essentially suggests that Lumentum hasn't put all of its eggs in the same basket.
Diversified Product Portfolio In addition to geographical and customer diversification, Lumentum also manufactures a diverse range of networking hardware that minimizes its cyclicality risk. For instance, Applied Optoelectronics mostly sells lasers and transceivers which makes its financial performance more or less correlated to the market demand for these two broad component categories at any given time, making it a highly cyclical stock.
But Lumentum has a wide range of product offerings that span from optical transceivers, tunable transmission modules, ROADMs, optical white boxes, industrial lasers along with diode lasers. Note that each listed category has sub categories within them, and each of the subcategories targets a separate niche in themselves. So, this product diversity tends to stabilize its overall sales.
Now, Lumentum provides only a broad segregation of revenues so we can't really see how each of the categories have been faring individually over time. But looking at the company's broadly-defined segment-level performance reveals that the company has been making balanced progress of late.
(Source: BusinessQuant.com)
Looking at the optical communications sector on a granular level provides us with another perspective. The company's consumer and industrial laser sub-segment has taken off quite substantially over the past couple of quarters. This segment mostly comprises of 3D sensing laser diode sales which became a hot selling commodity for the company ever since Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) started using it in its latest flagship, the iPhone X.
(Source: BusinessQuant.com)
Final thoughts Lumentum is a well-diversified company that has spread its bets across various customers, operating in a myriad of industries and located in different geographical regions. This has allowed the company to grow in a stable manner over the past several quarters now, and the trend may very well continue over the coming years as well, at least until something changes drastically. So, I believe that investing into Lumentum is a good way to gain exposure to the optical hardware segment for balanced growth, but without the volatility of its smaller pure-play peers.
